title: Hidden Markov Models
interviewAnswer: An HMM models a sequence with hidden states that follow Markov transitions and emit observations. Forward-backward computes marginals/likelihoods, Viterbi finds the most likely state path, and Baum–Welch learns parameters.
why: HMMs are foundational probabilistic sequence models used in speech, bioinformatics and state estimation.
intuition: You observe noisy outputs but assume an unobserved state evolves over time.
deepDive: The Markov assumption enables dynamic programming. Forward recursion sums over state paths; Viterbi replaces summation with maximization to recover the best path.
commonMistakes: Using Viterbi when marginal state probabilities are required.
followUps: How is Baum–Welch related to EM?
production: HMMs are interpretable and efficient baselines, but their assumptions can be too restrictive for complex sequences.
workedExample: A machine can move through healthy/degraded/failing hidden states while vibration measurements are noisy emissions.
